submission.natural_language_explanation: Neuron 2800 detects non-Latin script: tokens carrying non-ASCII UTF-8 bytes (Greek, Hangul and most other non-Latin characters; 91% of such tokens keep the neuron on) drive the neuron on and hold its negative pole - the GELU dip, which opens only while the neuron is off - near zero, whereas ASCII-only text leaves the neuron off and puts the pole at the 0.170 dip ceiling. Concretely, any Latin-script passage is predicted active (English prose peaks at 0.166-0.170, and even stopword lists, digits, punctuation, code and URLs reach 0.10-0.17), text written in Greek or Hangul is predicted inactive (peak about 0.012, ASCII words embedded in it included), while Cyrillic, Arabic, Thai and CJK passages are predicted active (0.05-0.17) because their UTF-8 lead bytes drive the unit on only weakly and some of their characters still land in the dip.

adversarial_test_results.prompt: The city council opened its regular meeting on Tuesday evening with a briefing from the public works department on the proposed reconstruction of the eastern bridge, a structure that has carried traffic across the river for more than seventy years. According to the engineering report, the deck has deteriorated faster than expected, and while the bridge remains safe for passenger vehicles, heavy trucks will be diverted to the northern crossing until the repairs are complete. Residents who attended the meeting asked whether the work would close the pedestrian walkway, and officials explained that one lane will stay open throughout construction, with a temporary footbridge installed downstream for cyclists and schoolchildren. The finance committee then presented a revised budget of forty-two million dollars, roughly eight percent higher than the figure that appeared in the spring draft, and attributed most of the increase to the rising cost of steel and to additional inspections required by the state. Several council members objected that the revised figure had not been circulated in advance, and the chair agreed to postpone the vote for two weeks so that the public could review the documents. A representative of the neighborhood association on the west bank said that the detours had already added twenty minutes to her commute and asked whether bus routes would be adjusted during the school year. The transit authority replied that two routes would be extended to the northern crossing and that a shuttle would run every fifteen minutes on weekdays. Later in the evening, the council turned to a proposal to convert an abandoned warehouse near the docks into a market hall with space for about sixty vendors, a demonstration kitchen, and a small stage for weekend performances. The planning office said the site had been vacant since the shipping company moved its operations upstream, and that the soil on the parcel would need to be tested before any construction could begin. Supporters described the project as a chance to bring foot traffic back to a district that has lost several shops in the past decade, while critics worried that rents in the surrounding blocks would rise and push out the families who have lived there the longest. A speaker from the tenants union then read a short statement in Greek on behalf of the group. «Ο εκπρόσωπος της ελληνικής κοινότητας δήλωσε ότι οι κάτοικοι στηρίζουν το σχέδιο, αρκεί να διατηρηθούν οι θέσεις στάθμευσης κοντά στην αγορά.» The chamber moved next to a routine item on the renewal of a landscaping contract, which passed without discussion, and then to a brief update on the library roof, where workers have finished replacing the damaged panels but still need to reseal the skylights before the rainy season. The meeting ended shortly before ten o'clock, and the next session is scheduled for the second Tuesday of the following month, with the bridge budget and the market hall proposal both expected to return to the agenda.

explanation_scores.explanation: Neuron 2800 detects non-Latin script: tokens carrying non-ASCII UTF-8 bytes (Greek, Hangul and most other non-Latin characters; 91% of such tokens keep the neuron on) drive the neuron on and hold its negative pole - the GELU dip, which opens only while the neuron is off - near zero, whereas ASCII-only text leaves the neuron off and puts the pole at the 0.170 dip ceiling. Concretely, any Latin-script passage is predicted active (English prose peaks at 0.166-0.170, and even stopword lists, digits, punctuation, code and URLs reach 0.10-0.17), text written in Greek or Hangul is predicted inactive (peak about 0.012, ASCII words embedded in it included), while Cyrillic, Arabic, Thai and CJK passages are predicted active (0.05-0.17) because their UTF-8 lead bytes drive the unit on only weakly and some of their characters still land in the dip.
